title: Operational Icons
slide_intent: Make small product symbols simple and consistent so staff and customers can identify ingredients quickly.
strategic_value: Illustration-derived icons can extend Burger King character into practical packaging information without sacrificing recognition.
demonstration: A left instruction column accompanies a four-row array of brown ingredient and operational symbols with captions, including cheese, patties, sauces, egg and abbreviated combinations.
practical_value: Use consistent-height operational icons between 24 and 84 pt, with the product-category color on white packaging.

content_islands.name: Icon guidance
content_islands.spec: Place the style rationale, size interval and white-background color rule at left.

content_islands.name: Ingredient grid
content_islands.spec: Arrange captioned ingredient and container icons in orderly rows across the right.

content_islands.name: Combination symbols
content_islands.spec: Retain the egg, EC and S specimens on the bottom row as part of the operational vocabulary.

reference_purposes.Intent: The text links the updated illustration-inspired style to bolder, simpler and instantly identifiable icons.
reference_purposes.Expression: The array demonstrates solid, irregular food silhouettes.
reference_purposes.Application: The page gives operational icon sizes and the product-category color treatment for white packaging.
reference_purposes.Constraint: Icons must remain at a consistent height, no larger than 84 pt and no smaller than 24 pt.

ingredient.name: Operational icons
ingredient.role: Identify products and ingredients on packaging.
ingredient.application: Keep a consistent height between 24 and 84 pt. On white packaging, use the product category’s primary color, such as Flaming Orange for chicken.
ingredient.scope: Historical operational packaging icons; these point sizes do not apply to the separate digital-icon rule.
